subject: a data analysis GUI using shiny?

messages.author: a814dd0eade31e3e
messages.subject: a data analysis GUI using shiny?
parts:
When I saw Winston's 'height/weight' application linked below built using Shiny the concept reminded me of plotbuilder in terms of how interactive it is. I used Deducer and JGR in class this quarter and students were very positive (Thanks Ian!!!!). However, when there were problems it always seemed to be with JGR. 

Based on what I have seen of Shiny sofar I think I could turn each of the tools I used in the class into a Shiny app. I'd want students to run the apps on their own laptop so they could do data analysis for assignments and cases. However, how would you combine all the applications into a menu structure? I have about 15 'tools' in the menu I use so tabs in one app/page would not be practical.

I could create an HTML based menu that students could put on their Desktops but can you 'call' or 'start' Shiny apps from the browser? Could the apps start on different ports perhaps (e.g., 8100 for the first, 8101 for the second, etc.)? I am imagining a system call to R with something like 'shiny::runApp('conjoint',8102).

Is something like this possible in the current version of Shiny or likely to be possible in a future release?

http://glimmer.rstudio.com/winston/heightweight/

messages.author: ca443e6eaa0e78ed
messages.subject: Re: a data analysis GUI using shiny?
parts:
Hi Vincent,

Yes, I'd create an HTML based menu (frameset or iframe based?) that displays the apps. To host the apps themselves you have the following options:
  1. The second argument to runApp is indeed port number. So yes, you could start 15 apps on different ports if you wanted to. You probably then also want to pass the "launch.browser=FALSE" argument so 15 browsers don't spawn!
  2. The glimmer.rstudio.com server that you pointed to is available for public beta testing (it's free during beta testing but is likely to become a paid service at some point). You can register by going to http://rstudio.com/shiny/ and clicking the "register now" link near the bottom.
  3. In late January we'll be releasing the software that runs on glimmer.rstudio.com for beta testing, so you can run it on your own server (Linux required, for the first version at least).
Hope that helps.

messages.author: a814dd0eade31e3e
messages.subject: Re: a data analysis GUI using shiny?
parts:
Thanks for the input Joe! I haven't done much of programming on this yet. I have been thinking about how to setup the menu-structure but I am still not sure how to best do this.

Setting up the menu in HTML and then creating the analysis dialogs as shiny apps seems feasible. However, starting 15 separate Shiny processes seems a bit clunky. 

I think I could also setup a menu in JGR/Deducer although that might be overkill. I even thought about setting up the menu in Sublime Edit 2 (SE2). This editor use XML to build menu's (see link) below. 

That made me wonder if something like what SE2 allows might be a possible add-on for Rstudio. The user could specify an XML file with menu labels. The menu items would then simply call shiny apps and start them in a browser as needed.

Does that make any sense?

http://www.sublimetext.com/docs/menus

PS I know there have been requests to integrate Rstudio and Deducer but I assume that would be a lot more complicated.

messages.author: a814dd0eade31e3e
messages.subject: Re: a data analysis GUI using shiny?
parts:
I put a partially-working hack of a data-analysis menu using shiny on github (https://github.com/mostly-harmless/damshiny.git)

As you will see there is not that much there just yet. I see it as a 'proof-of-concept' of what I am trying for. I also posted the files as a Gist. The following should work, if not please let me know.

library(shiny)
shiny::runGist('4385800')

I have a number of questions and would love to hear suggestions on how to do this better. If you would like to contribute directly, even better.

1. I used fileInput to allow a user to load data. I couldn't determine how to get ui.R and server.R to use the file however.
2. I'd also like a list of data.frames available for analysis. The 'is.data.frame' code on lines 4 and 5 seems to work outside of the app but not inside.
3. How to create a vector of variable names from the selected dataset that can be used in model specification? 
3. Is using 'conditionalPanel' the way go here? Is there a way to avoid putting the if(input$tool == '') arguments in each reactive function separately? I got an error when I tried to put the if-statement around a set of reactives.
4. What about an html form with GET (e.g., localhost:8100?tool=reg)? How would you setup the if-statements to get the desired inputs and outputs to show?
5. For the comparison of means the Correlation tab could be dropped. I saw some discussion about this but it wasn't clear to me how to implement the suggestions.
6. Plots don't show completely (have to scroll). Is there a way to make the output window longer?
7. For larger datasets I might want to turn-off reactive features. Is that possible and if so how?
